title: Fix the Broken Config
description: Each config is broken in a way people really break theirs. Find the bug, fix it with as few keys as possible.

intro: These bugs break real configs, often without an error message. A config runs top to bottom, each line seeing only what came before it, and most mistakes come from that order or from a value of the wrong kind in the wrong place.

commands.text: <leader> is read when a mapping is made. Set vim.g.mapleader before any mapping that uses it, or those mappings keep the default leader, \.
An option takes a Lua value of its own type: vim.o.tabstop = 4, not "4".
A mapping that starts with : types into the command line, so it needs <CR> at the end to run, or use <cmd>...<CR>.
vim.g sets a global variable, which only plugins read. Options are set with vim.o.
A command made with nvim_create_user_command must start with a capital letter.

levels.title: Leader too late
levels.description: <leader>w should save, with <Space> as the leader. Both lines are right; something else is wrong.
levels.hint: <leader> is read when the mapping is made, so the leader must be set first.

levels.title: Type error
levels.description: This config fails to load. Make 'shiftwidth' 2.
levels.hint: Number options take Lua numbers, not strings.

levels.title: Missing enter
levels.hint: A ':' mapping types into the command line; it needs a <CR> at the end to run.

levels.title: vim.g is not vim.o
levels.description: Line numbers never show up. The config loads without errors; it just sets the wrong thing.
levels.hint: vim.g sets a global variable (g:number), which nothing reads. Options live in vim.o.

levels.title: Mind the case
levels.description: This config fails to load. :Trim should strip trailing whitespace.
levels.hint: User command names must start with an uppercase letter. ~ flips the case of a character.
